faq.a: Beyond basic needs like food, shelter, and safety, what’s essential is the small set of things you couldn’t lose without losing yourself. For most people that includes close relationships, health, core values, and a sense of purpose.

faq.q: How do I figure out what is essential to me?
faq.a: Imagine losing each part of your life and notice how you’d feel, look at what your best days had in common, and ask what you’d protect if you had to cut your commitments in half.

faq.q: What’s the difference between essential and important?
faq.a: Essential things are load-bearing for who you are. Important things support those essentials, like income or rest, but aren’t the core themselves.

faq.q: Is focusing on essentials the same as minimalism?
faq.a: Not exactly. Minimalism often focuses on owning less, while focusing on essentials starts with values and applies to time, energy, and relationships too.

faq.q: How many essentials should I have?
faq.a: Keep your list short, around five to seven items. A short list works as a filter for decisions, while a long list becomes a wish list.

faq.q: Do my essentials change over time?
faq.a: Yes. Life stages, responsibilities, and values shift, so it helps to revisit your list each season or after major changes.
